analysis.title: Trembling Taiwan
key_insights: The TWII (Taiwan index) has fallen around 8% in the week since The Market Ear's bearish Taiwan note 'The next AI domino'. It broke its trend line overnight and closed well below the 100-day moving average, with little real support until the 200-day moving average.
Taiwan is trading at its most oversold levels since the Liberation Day selloff. The Market Ear calls it the 'last man standing' among AI-linked markets to fall.
KOSPI led both the move higher and the move down. KOSPI has held its recent lows, while SOX and Taiwan are catching down and narrowing the performance gap with Korea.

BofA's chart shows Taiwan far above the rest of Asia in AI trade exposure relative to GDP, while Taiwan remains a net energy importer. A moderation in global AI spending could hit Taiwan disproportionately, especially with energy costs elevated.

ANZ highlights the historical relationship between Taiwan's exports and the SOX. Semiconductor performance can give an early signal for export momentum, so the risk is that equity weakness spills into the real economy.

The EWT December 95 put has more than doubled since last week's note, before today's 2.5% pre-market decline in EWT. With Taiwan extremely oversold, The Market Ear suggests booking some profits and rolling into lower-strike puts while keeping some downside convexity.

sector_views.rationale: Taiwan's exports track the SOX, and the report flags significant semiconductor volatility as a risk to Taiwan's real economy and equities.

trade_ideas.description: Book partial profits on the EWT December 95 put and roll into lower-strike EWT puts, keeping some downside convexity
trade_ideas.rationale: The put has more than doubled and Taiwan is extremely oversold, so the report suggests monetizing part of the move.
trade_ideas.risk: Taiwan is extremely oversold, which raises the risk of a bounce.

risk_factors: Taiwan has the highest AI trade exposure relative to GDP in Asia, so any moderation in global AI spending could hit it disproportionately.
Taiwan is a net energy importer and energy costs remain elevated.
Taiwan's exports depend on the global semiconductor cycle, so weakness in the SOX could spill into the real economy if the chip cycle loses momentum.
vol_and_positioning: Taiwan is at its most oversold levels since the Liberation Day selloff, and the TWII closed well below its 100-day moving average.
The EWT December 95 put has more than doubled since last week. EWT was down 2.5% pre-market today.
KOSPI has held its recent lows while SOX and Taiwan continue to catch down, narrowing the performance gap with Korea.

Last week's idea was to treat the put as a lottery ticket and let the convexity work if Taiwan caught down. The report now suggests taking partial profits and rolling into lower-strike puts, keeping some downside convexity.

ANZ highlights the historical relationship between Taiwan's exports and the SOX.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI boom has delivered extraordinary growth, and Taiwan's macro strength is extraordinary.
tension_points.bear_case: Taiwan has the most AI exposure relative to GDP in Asia and is a net energy importer. Any moderation in global AI spending, or a chip cycle slowdown showing up in SOX, could hit exports and the economy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Semiconductor performance, via the SOX-to-exports relationship, is the signal to watch. A recovery in the SOX would weaken the bear case, while further SOX weakness would confirm it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Taiwan is the AI trade's most concentrated market and is catching down to SOX and KOSPI weakness.
theme_stances.evidence: The last man standing has finally fallen.
